subject: general
question: As per the Economic Survey, 2024–25, what is the global movement led by India to promote sustainable lifestyles called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**LiFE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **LiFE** stands for **Lifestyle for Environment**, a global movement led by **India** to promote sustainable lifestyles.
 
• It was introduced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** during the **2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP26)** held in **Glasgow, Scotland**.
 
• The initiative emphasizes the importance of **mindful and deliberate utilization of resources**, moving away from mindless consumption.
 
• The concept of LiFE encourages people to adopt sustainable practices in their daily lives, such as reducing waste, conserving energy, and using environmentally friendly products.
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024–25** reiterates the importance of LiFE in combating **climate change** and achieving the goals of a **net-zero economy** by reducing carbon emissions through individual and collective actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of LiFE:**

 
 
• LiFE was conceptualized by India as part of its commitment to global environmental sustainability and was formally proposed by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** at COP26 in **November 2021**.
 
• The initiative aligns with the principles of the **Paris Agreement** to limit global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of LiFE:**
 
 
• Encouraging individuals to adopt sustainable practices to reduce their carbon footprint.
 
• Promoting circular economy principles, such as **reuse, recycle, and repair**.
 
• Advocating for policies that support sustainable production and consumption patterns globally.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact of LiFE:**
 
 
• LiFE aims to create a **mass movement** for sustainable living by involving governments, businesses, and individuals worldwide.
 
• The movement emphasizes that climate action is not limited to governments and industries but also requires individual contributions.
 
• Countries and organizations worldwide have shown interest in collaborating with India on this initiative to tackle global environmental challenges.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of LiFE:**
 
 
• Focus on **behavioral change** to encourage environmentally conscious choices.
 
• Promotion of **eco-friendly technologies** and products.
 
• Integration of sustainability into **education systems** to raise awareness among younger generations.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role in Global Climate Action:**
 
 
• As a signatory to the **Paris Agreement**, India has committed to reducing its carbon intensity by 33-35% by 2030 (compared to 2005 levels).
 
• India is actively working towards achieving its **net-zero emissions target by 2070**.
 
• The LiFE movement complements India’s other initiatives, such as the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** and the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Earth First:** A general term often used in environmental movements but not a specific initiative led by India.
 
• **Go Green:** A phrase promoting environmental consciousness but not related to the LiFE initiative.
 
• **Swachh Life:** This term might sound related to cleanliness drives like **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, but it is not the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements:**
 
 
• India’s efforts under LiFE have received international recognition for promoting **sustainable living**.
 
• The movement has inspired various global organizations to incorporate sustainability into their operations.
 
 
 
• **Link to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• LiFE aligns with SDG 12 (**Responsible Consumption and Production**) and SDG 13 (**Climate Action**).
 
• It also contributes to SDG 7 (**Affordable and Clean Energy**) by promoting energy-efficient practices.
